author: first_agent
question: Is the inboard position of our MAST plasma an artefact of the house Picard solve, or does an independent free-boundary solver driven by the same inputs put the plasma in the same place?
rule_3: MAST inputs only (coil currents incl. the solenoid convention of fec_adapter.machine, Ip, TF current, Thomson); machine geometry (vessel envelope as wall). No MAST equilibrium field, demo shot or leaderboard number.
solver: FreeGS commit 9fbec2056b4322ea253bb5614896d549365163f3 (LGPL-3.0, the second agent's isolated checkout and venv, unchanged), setup as second_agent run_freegs_actual_mast_vessel_20260929.py: every input coil a FilamentCoil at its measured current, wall = vessel envelope contour, organisers' MAST 65x65 grid extent, profiles ConstrainPaxisIp(p_axis, Ip, F_vacuum) with FreeGS default exponents, check_limited True, maxits 50.
p_axis: 2.25 x electron pressure at the Thomson profile peak (3 cm Gaussian smoothing, as v7) - the DIII-D-calibrated factor, label-free.
sample: shots 0, 301, 603, 904, 1205 (sorted stream order, the second agent's feasibility set) x frames at 25/50/75 % of the live window (|Ip| >= 300 kA and a Te 5 % marker on both sides) = up to 15 frames.
metrics: LCFS midplane crossings at the laser height by the organisers' reading (Reader('MAST')) of the FreeGS map and of our v7 map; minus the Thomson Te 5 % marker moved by the DIII-D calibration (out +1.7 cm, in -1.7 cm); solved Ip / input Ip.
decision_rule: If FreeGS's median outboard marker error is at least 2 cm smaller than v7's on the same frames (and converged frames >= 10 of 15), the position error is a house-solver artefact -> build the full FreeGS pilot (M3c). If not, both solvers place the plasma alike from the same inputs -> the cause is in the inputs' treatment (coil/solenoid/passive), recorded, and the FreeGS route is not pursued for position.
